title: stall-resistant-load-trimmer: dynamic slow-path admission + tenant rebalancer (hotfix)
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Hotfix: add adaptive slow-path admission controller and tenant rebalancer to reduce prolonged stalls during regional surges; exposes new metrics and console views for investigating slow drains
description:
Context and motivation: This hotfix addresses a production incident (INC-2026-02-17) where a subset of requests entered a slow-path admission queue and failed to make forward progress when regional egress saturated. Root cause analysis pointed to two contributing issues: (1) admission controller thresholds were static and tuned for steady-state load, not surge transitions; (2) tenant-aware rebalancing logic did not preemptively nudge long-running KV drains, leading to longer-than-expected stall times for some lanes. The regression surfaced in late-night traffic spike and caused degraded p99 tail latency for a handful of tenants.

Summary of changes (single continuous description): Implement an adaptive slow-path admission controller that tracks moving-window service-time distributions and adjusts admission cutoffs dynamically; introduce a tenant rebalancer that detects sticky drains and issues light-weight eviction hints to accelerate KV cache handoff for affected tenants; add a soft-eviction decay that gradually reduces penalties for tenants after successful graceful retries to avoid permanent demotion; wire additional telemetry (runtime.slowpath.admissions, runtime.tenant.rebalance_attempts, runtime.slowpath.drain_time_histogram) and a Console dashboard snapshot for on-call triage; include an integration test harness and a focused load test to reproduce the stall pattern seen in INC-2026-02-17. This PR is intended as a hotfix with minimal behavioral change outside surge scenarios.

- [x] Added observability (metrics + dashboard) for on-call
- [x] Back-compat ensured (soft-eviction decay is opt-in via flag until rollout)

Design notes / reasoning: The adaptive admission controller uses an exponential moving window over service times and recent drain events to avoid reacting to single outliers; thresholds are bumped conservatively and include a minimum holdoff to prevent oscillation. Tenant rebalancer is intentionally lightweight: it only emits a soft eviction hint (idempotent and advisory) which the runtime uses to prioritize background KV handoff; it does not forcibly evict or drop in-flight requests. Soft-eviction decay avoids permanently lowering tenant priority after transient problems.

Testing: Added deterministic unit tests for estimator math and simulated integration tests that reproduce the original stall pattern with a controlled egress choke. CI matrix included linux/amd64 unit+integration. During CI we observed a flaky network test unrelated to changes; test was retried and passed on second run. All checks green at merge time.

Review discussion (selected):
- Jordan Lee (review): "Adaptive thresholds look reasonable but we should add an explicit cooldown metric to detect oscillation." — Author reply: "Added runtime.slowpath.cooldown_count and a brief doc comment explaining cooldown semantics (commit 3)."
- Samir Gupta (review): "Tenant rebalancer needs to be non-blocking and should not introduce extra scheduling latency." — Author reply: "Rebalancer runs as background coroutine with bounded work per tick; added benchmarks (bench results in PR) showing <1% CPU impact under 10k qps." 
- Elena Park (review): "Prometheus labels need to include tenant_id fingerprinting policy." — Author reply: "Metrics will use tenant hash (non-reversible) to avoid PII; updated collector and tests."
- Jordan Lee (requested change): "Please gate the new behavior behind a feature flag for gradual rollout." — Author reply: "Done; flag exposed in helm values and default OFF for canary until rollout plan completed."
- Final approvals: Jordan Lee (approved), Samir Gupta (approved), Elena Park (approved).

CI summary: build: pass; unit tests: pass; integration: pass after 1 flake retry; lint: pass; e2e: skipped (hotfix, limited scope). Artifacts: integration logs and benchmark outputs attached to build #1229.

Merge decision: Hotfix approved by SRE and runtime leads. Merged via squash by Maya Thompson on 2026-02-20 after gating the feature flag false-by-default in production values. Post-merge actions: (1) deploy to canary region for 4 hours with enhanced telemetry; (2) run targeted load test to validate stall reduction; (3) if stable, flip rollout flag over 2 regional waves. Runbook and rollback steps included in docs/ops/load_trimmer.md. Link to incident summary: https://linear.app/redwood/incident/INC-2026-02-17-stall-pattern (internal).

Notes for future: Consider a coarse-grained global controller that can coordinate admission thresholds across regions for synchronous failures; add automated alert that correlates slowpath.admissions spike with region egress saturation to auto-trigger mitigation runbook.
